subcomponents.title: Verification tooling robustness

criteria.rationale: All six copies were inspected: the repository and bootstrap-template versions of verify.mjs, inspect-presentation.mjs and lib/project.mjs. The two versions of each file are identical. startPreview launches Vite's own bin/vite.js under process.execPath, so the child process is the preview server itself rather than an npm or npx wrapper. stop() sends SIGTERM, schedules SIGKILL after 3s, and awaits the child's 'exit' promise. votes.rationale: Neither credited mechanism is met. The port is ephemeral and --strictPort is used. But freePort closes its probe server before vite binds, so there is a window in which another server can take the port. Readiness then comes only from HTTP-polling `fetch(url/)` and accepting any `response.ok`, not from the child's own announcement of its address. The only ownership check is the `exited` flag sampled at the top of each loop iteration, before the request. A server that answers on that port before the child's exit is observed would be accepted as the preview. Polling is not raced against the child's exit, and the spawned child's stdout is never used for readiness.

readiness loop: `if (exited) throw ...` then `const response = await fetch(`${url}/`); if (response.ok) break`

`exit` is a promise used only by stop(), not raced against the readiness fetch

result.rationale: I'm ruling with judges A and C: pass. The helper supports an explicit allow-overlap marker, and a focused browser test confirms it. How it works: `collectSnapshot` (diagnostics.mjs:47-53) walks each element's ancestors and records the id of every ancestor that carries `data-presentation-allow-overlap` in `allow`. `findOverlaps` (diagnostics.mjs:96-109) skips any pair whose elements share one of those marked ancestors (`a.allow.some((id) => b.allow.includes(id))`). `analyzeSnapshot` (127-131) only reports pairs that `findOverlaps` returns. `inspect-presentation.mjs` (52-62) runs the snapshot and analysis on every step, after the settle wait. Focused test: inspect.test.ts builds the `fx-allowed` fixture (line 31). It puts two Labels at identical coordinates inside `<div data-presentation-allow-overlap>`. The test 'does not report overlap inside an explicitly allowed subtree' (147-151) runs the real helper against a production build and asserts exit 0 with no WARN lines. The same Labels without the marker (`fx-collision`) do produce a warning naming both texts (137-145), so the marker is what suppresses it. The unit test 'exempts pairs inside one allow-overlap subtree only' (diagnostics.test.ts:26-34) checks the same thing at the function level: a marked pair produces no warning, and the identical pair without the marker produces one. Why I'm not ruling with judge B: the material is accurate but does not decide this requirement. B points out that a marked element colliding with an unmarked one is still reported, and diagnostics.test.ts:32 confirms that. But the review guidance only says skipping every pair with at least one marked element is "a correct reading". It says "do not require the helper to keep reporting collisions between a marked element and an unmarked one", which makes the one-sided skip acceptable, not mandatory. B misquotes this as "the correct reading". The fixture scenario is overlap between elements inside the marked subtree. Those collisions are suppressed and tested, and the guidance's requirement is a focused test that marks an overlapping subtree and gets no warning, which exists. Nothing cited shows the candidate's own presentation producing a marked-versus-unmarked collision.

votes.rationale: I read every non-test kit file, including the primitives Box, Label, SymbolChip, Frame, Emphasis, Node, Arrow, Appear and SceneLayer. I also read the chrome (Header, Toc, Footer, Attribution), Stage and Presentation. None of them supplies a fallback color, font, border, shadow, card treatment or button treatment. The primitives Box, Label, SymbolChip and Frame all render through Node. Node sets only layout and motion props: `layout`, `layoutId`, `transition`, data hooks, and `rectStyle(at)`, which returns position/left/top/width/height only. Box and SymbolChip add only an optional Lucide icon carrying a `data-presentation-icon` hook. Frame adds only `pointerEvents: 'none'` and a hook-only label span. Emphasis adds only `pointerEvents: 'none'`. Arrow's SVG uses `currentColor` for stroke and fill, so it inherits the presentation's color rather than supplying one. Chrome inline styles are placement geometry only (position, offsets, size, flex alignment, overflow, nowrap/ellipsis). The Toc and Footer buttons are bare `<button>` elements with no kit styling. Appear and Stage use opacity and transform for motion and fit. The kit has no CSS files and adds no `className`. `src/presentation-kit/neutrality.test.tsx` backs this up. It renders Appear, Box, Label, Frame, Emphasis, SymbolChip and Arrow inside Presentation, and it asserts that no element has a class. It also asserts that every inline style property is in a layout-only allowlist. I did not run it, and no recorded result is cited here. My verdict rests on the source reading above.

votes.rationale: Neither credited mechanism is met. The port is ephemeral and --strictPort is used. But freePort closes its probe server before vite binds, so there is a window in which another server can take the port. Readiness then comes only from HTTP-polling `fetch(url/)` and accepting any `response.ok`, not from the child's own announcement of its address. The only ownership check is the `exited` flag sampled at the top of each loop iteration, before the request. A server that answers on that port before the child's exit is observed would be accepted as the preview. Polling is not raced against the child's exit, and the spawned child's stdout is never used for readiness.
evidence: startPreview: `const port = await freePort()`, then spawn vite with --strictPort
readiness loop: `if (exited) throw ...` then `const response = await fetch(`${url}/`); if (response.ok) break`
`log` is collected from stdout/stderr but never parsed for a ready/address announcement
`exit` is a promise used only by stop(), not raced against the readiness fetch

votes.rationale: Readiness comes from HTTP polling of a port that was reserved and then released, not from the child's own announcement of its address. first_results.rationale: I'm ruling with judges A and C: pass. The helper supports an explicit allow-overlap marker, and a focused browser test confirms it. How it works: `collectSnapshot` (diagnostics.mjs:47-53) walks each element's ancestors and records the id of every ancestor that carries `data-presentation-allow-overlap` in `allow`. `findOverlaps` (diagnostics.mjs:96-109) skips any pair whose elements share one of those marked ancestors (`a.allow.some((id) => b.allow.includes(id))`). `analyzeSnapshot` (127-131) only reports pairs that `findOverlaps` returns. `inspect-presentation.mjs` (52-62) runs the snapshot and analysis on every step, after the settle wait. Focused test: inspect.test.ts builds the `fx-allowed` fixture (line 31). It puts two Labels at identical coordinates inside `<div data-presentation-allow-overlap>`. The test 'does not report overlap inside an explicitly allowed subtree' (147-151) runs the real helper against a production build and asserts exit 0 with no WARN lines. The same Labels without the marker (`fx-collision`) do produce a warning naming both texts (137-145), so the marker is what suppresses it. The unit test 'exempts pairs inside one allow-overlap subtree only' (diagnostics.test.ts:26-34) checks the same thing at the function level: a marked pair produces no warning, and the identical pair without the marker produces one. Why I'm not ruling with judge B: the material is accurate but does not decide this requirement. B points out that a marked element colliding with an unmarked one is still reported, and diagnostics.test.ts:32 confirms that. But the review guidance only says skipping every pair with at least one marked element is "a correct reading". It says "do not require the helper to keep reporting collisions between a marked element and an unmarked one", which makes the one-sided skip acceptable, not mandatory. B misquotes this as "the correct reading". The fixture scenario is overlap between elements inside the marked subtree. Those collisions are suppressed and tested, and the guidance's requirement is a focused test that marks an overlapping subtree and gets no warning, which exists. Nothing cited shows the candidate's own presentation producing a marked-versus-unmarked collision.

audit_results.rationale: The requirement is met. When a presentation marks a subtree with `data-presentation-allow-overlap`, the helper does not report overlaps between elements inside it. A focused test marks an overlapping subtree and asserts that no warning comes back. How the code does it: - `collectSnapshot` (diagnostics.mjs:47-53) records which marked ancestors each element has. - `findOverlaps` (diagnostics.mjs:104) skips any pair that shares a marked ancestor. - `analyzeSnapshot` (127-131) only warns about pairs that `findOverlaps` returns. - `inspect-presentation.mjs` (52-62) runs the snapshot and the analysis on every step. The tests: - **Integration test:** `fx-allowed` (inspect.test.ts:31) puts two Labels at identical positions inside a marked div, and the test at 147-151 asserts exit 0 with no WARN lines. `fx-collision` (137-145) uses the same Labels without the marker and gets a warning naming both texts, so the marker is what suppresses it. - **Unit test:** diagnostics.test.ts:26-30 checks the same thing directly on `findOverlaps`. The child process is therefore the preview server itself, not an npm or npx wrapper. stop() sends SIGTERM, falls back to SIGKILL after 3s and awaits the child's 'exit' promise. In verify.mjs, main wraps everything after startPreview in try/finally { await preview.stop() }. launchBrowser runs inside renderRoute, which runs inside that try. In inspect-presentation.mjs, a launchBrowser rejection is caught and awaits preview.stop() before rethrowing. All later work runs inside try/finally { await browser.close(); await preview.stop() }. first_results.rationale: The coverage requirement is met. The round-0 pass record works through the product's public surfaces for almost every basis scenario, and each item records what was done and what was seen. - **Reference sample (production preview):** step model, titles and captions, numbering, node identity across steps, newcomer opacity at the key press and after settle, and departure timing in a fault copy. It also covers grouped scenes, intentional composition, attribution and brand slot, present and browse modes, the mode toggle, keyboard, synthetic swipe, direct jump, active state, control keys, both clamps, and uniform scaling with the default canvas. - **Scaffold:** empty, already-scaffolded, partial, monorepo, standalone, incompatible-dependency and cwd-independence journeys. It also covers creating a presentation and preserving existing ones. - **`npm run verify`:** a clean pass and fault runs for build failure, missing sample, out-of-order steps, a console error that names its step, and a stalled transition. - **`npm run inspect`:** capture plus the overlap, allow-overlap, active-chrome and attribution warnings. Round 2 re-explored the changed seam (the sample footer CSS) at 480, 360 and 320 px across all nine steps. It also checked the breakpoint and vertical fit. Judge C's vote (fail) does not decide the requirement. C says the conversational omissions (Floor G) are not shown to be environmental, but the record states the impediment. The plan says these items "require a live agent session following `SKILL.md`; this pass drove the deterministic scaffold helper, not the dialogue". The log repeats per item that each one is "a model dialogue following `SKILL.md`". That is the criterion's own example of an environmental gap: a skill journey that needs a separate agent invocation the environment does not provide. Under the criterion, such disclosed items do not count against coverage. Even so, the tool-level gates behind them were exercised: the `needsConfirmation` flag, non-zero exits with named phases, and warnings with step numbers. The animation limits are disclosed: there was no frame-by-frame check by eye, and mid-transition opacity was not sampled finely. So are the remaining product omissions, such as physical touch and widths other than those tested. Those left unexercised are small compared with what was covered. Judges A and B's pass is borne out.

lines.text: ### Floor A: reference sample walkthrough (production preview, 127.0.0.1)

- **Scene step model, identity, titles and captions.** Predicted: nine steps with the spec table's titles and captions, in order. Observed: `steps.ts` and the rendered headings match the spec table verbatim for all nine steps (checked the `BEATS` array against the spec table, and the `h2` and caption text per step in the DOM). Result: pass.

- **Order-derived numbering.** Predicted: number equals position. Observed: the header number and progress item track `nav.index + 1` (`Presentation.tsx:36`). Reorder check (step 8, below): swapping two steps in a copy produced `step 0 Second beat`, `step 1 First beat`, and verify passed. Result: pass.

- **Stable entities morph; newcomers enter after settle; departing entity exits.** Predicted: persisting entities keep their DOM node; newcomers fade in after the ~0.65 s delay; departures fade out. Observed (DOM node identity and opacity across all nine transitions): persisting nodes were kept (same element) at every transition; newcomers were created fresh with opacity 0 right after the press and 1.00 after settling. Departure was not exercised by the sample itself (the sample never removes an entity). Departure was exercised in copy `faultC` (entity `first` removed from step 2 onward): the mutation log showed `first` at opacity 1.00 at t+0 ms, fading to 0.00 at about +260 ms, then removed from the DOM, while `second` stayed at 1.00. Result: pass for departure timing; the sample has no departure beat.

- **Grouped scene shares one instance.** Predicted: one `groupKey` and one `Scene` keep persisting entities mounted across steps. Observed: persisting nodes were never remounted across steps 1 to 9 (node identity probe). Result: pass.

- **Continuing entities are not faded as newcomers.** Predicted: persisting entities stay at full opacity while moving. Observed: opacity 1.00 for every continuing entity at every settled step. The mid-transition value for continuing entities was not sampled finely enough to rule out a brief dip. Result: pass at the settled level; the wrapper question is recorded in the ledger.

- **Intentional composition preserved.** Observed: step 6 places the scene-kit socket under the tray (not framed), step 7 chains `verify` in the tray row with a `pass` chip, step 9 draws the frame. Screenshots `wide-step6.png`, `wide-step9.png`. Result: pass by inspection.

- **Attribution: bottom-right, labelled, linked; no top-left brand.** Observed: link `made by and-scene` to `https://github.com/Codagent-AI/and-scene` at bottom-right (screenshots); brand slot empty (`data-presentation-brand-slot` has no content). Result: pass.

- **Present and browse modes.** Predicted: present shows marker and title only; browse shows caption, ToC on wide, controls, progress. Observed (step 6, blurred focus, `p` key): present has marker `6` and title `It assembles the scene`, and no caption, ToC, controls, or progress elements. Browse restores them. Screenshot `s5-present.png`. Result: pass.
- **Mode toggle keeps position.** Observed: step index 5 before and after toggle (present and back). Result: pass.
- **Keyboard navigation.** Predicted: Right, Space, PageDown advance; Left, PageUp go back. Observed: Right 0→1, Space 1→2, PageDown 2→3, Left 3→2, PageUp 2→1. Result: pass.

- **Touch swipe.** Predicted: horizontal left swipe advances, right goes back, vertical does nothing. Observed (synthetic `TouchEvent` with `Touch` objects dispatched on `window`): left swipe 5→6, right swipe 6→5, mostly-vertical gesture 5→5. Result: pass. Synthetic input stands in for a touchscreen (permitted substitute).

- **Direct jump.** Predicted: progress item jumps to that step; ToC entry jumps to the first step of that era. Observed (real clicks through AXI refs): ToC `the reveal`→8, `the gathering`→2, `the loop`→7; progress `Step 8`→7, `Step 1`→0, `Step 2`→1. Result: pass. (Note: an early progress click used a malformed uid and did nothing; it was retried with a fresh snapshot. This was a tooling error on my side, not a product failure.)

- **Active navigation state exposed.** Observed: ToC active entry has `aria-current="true"` and `data-presentation-active`; progress active item has `aria-current="step"` and `data-presentation-active`; both track the current era or step. Result: pass.

- **Controls keep their keys.** Predicted: Space or Enter on a focused Next advances once; Space on a focused progress item jumps only; arrows on a focused progress item do not also advance. Observed: focused Next + Space 0→1 (once); focused Next + Enter 1→2 (once); focused progress item + ArrowRight 2→2; focused progress item + Space jumped to 0 (once). Result: pass. The `p` key is ignored while focus is on a button; see ledger entry "P key ignored while focus is on a control".
- **Boundary clamp.** Observed: 10 × Right from step 1 stayed at index 8 (step 9), 11 × Left stayed at 0. Next button disabled on step 9, Previous disabled on step 1. Result: pass.

- **Fixed-canvas uniform scaling.** Observed: at 1280 width the canvas scale is 1.20455 (both axes, matrix a=d); at 480 width scale 0.545455 (uniform), canvas width 480 px. No reflow in either. Result: pass for scaling. Legibility at 480 is a separate concern (ledger).
- **Default canvas 880 × 380.** Observed: canvas rendered width 1060 px ÷ 1.20455 = 880; height 457.7 ÷ 1.20455 = 380. Result: pass.

- **Kit style boundary (no default colours, fonts, borders in the kit).** Code-read: `grep` of `src/presentation-kit` for color, font, border, background, shadow returned no matches. Observed: fault copy with a background-only `talk.css` rendered browser-default buttons and text with no kit fills (`fault-chrome-step-01.png`). Result: pass.
- **Kit primitives expose hooks.** Observed: nodes carry `data-presentation-node="box"` and `data-presentation-id` (overlap diagnostics print them). Result: pass.
Covered in Floor A (kit style boundary). Result: pass.
### Floor C: scaffold from an empty directory (`journeys/empty`)

- **Target and detection.** `detect` on the empty directory: target = the directory, reason `empty directory: scaffold at the root`, `needsConfirmation: false`, all three anchors missing. Result: pass.

- **Full scaffold with dependency install.** `apply --install` (exit 0): 49 template files copied (full JSON in `acceptance-logs/empty-apply.log`), all three anchors added, `package.json` with `lucide-react`, `motion`, `react`, `react-dom`, `typescript`, `vite`, `@vitejs/plugin-react`, `eslint`, `playwright`, `typescript-eslint`. Observed install: `added 168 packages`. Playwright chromium installation printed nothing, and `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/ms-playwright` is set in this environment; the later verify run launched Chromium successfully. Result: pass.

- **No styling framework.** No `tailwind` in templates or `package.json`; build passes. `src/index.css` contains only a `box-sizing` rule and a `body { margin: 0 }` reset (ledger). Result: pass with one ledger note.
- **Template resolution independent of cwd.** `detect` and `apply` run from `/artifacts/...` and from another directory with an absolute script path returned identical results. Result: pass.

- **Create a new presentation.** `new demo-talk "Demo Talk"` created `src/presentations/demo-talk/` (Scene.tsx, Talk.tsx, entities.ts, steps.ts, talk.css) and appended one registry entry. Build passed. `npm run verify -- demo-talk` passed (2 steps). Result: pass.
- **Presentation owns style.** `talk.css` is the plain-CSS file with `data-presentation-*` hooks; the kit has no such CSS. Result: pass.
- **Existing presentations preserved.** After adding `demo-talk`, `npm run verify -- starter` passed (2 steps); the registry kept `starter`. Result: pass.
### Floor D: already-scaffolded, partial, and monorepo

results.rationale: The approved inventory (packet.txt lines 42-226) lists about 64 scenarios across three documents. The verified round-0 pass record covers nearly all of them through public surfaces, with a prediction, observation and result for each. - **Requirement-001 (the presentation kit):** exercised in the production preview on 127.0.0.1. Covered: step titles and captions, order-derived numbering with a reorder check, persisting nodes kept across transitions, newcomers going from opacity 0 to 1 after settling, a departure fading out and being removed, grouped scenes updating in place, continuing entities staying at opacity 1, intentional composition, style hooks, unstyled kit output, attribution and the empty brand slot, present and browse modes, mode toggle keeping position, the keyboard keys, synthetic swipe, ToC and progress jumps, the active aria-current hooks, controls keeping their keys, clamping at both ends, uniform scaling at 1280 and 480 px, and the 880×380 canvas. - **Requirement-002 (the skill):** scaffold journeys for the empty, already-scaffolded, partial, monorepo, standalone and incompatible-dependency cases, plus template resolution from another cwd, no styling framework, `new` with registry append, and existing presentations preserved. - **Requirement-003 (verification):** a clean `verify` PASS with logs, plus build, missing-sample, out-of-order, console-error and transition fault runs. Also the inspect helper's capture, settled capture, overlap, allow-overlap, active-chrome and attribution warnings. - **Round 2:** re-explored the changed seam at 480, 360 and 320 px across all nine steps, plus the breakpoints and vertical fit. The one omitted group is Floor G: the conversational skill journeys (one-question gathering, partial detail, complete prompt, ASCII mockup, ambiguous and scoped modify, the repair loop as agent conduct, and the confirmation exchange). The record discloses this as "requires a live agent session following `SKILL.md`; this pass drove the deterministic scaffold helper, not the dialogue". That is the case the criterion names as environmental: a skill journey that needs a separate agent invocation the environment does not provide. So it does not count against coverage. Judge C argues that this is a scoping choice. Even on that reading, the omission is about 9 of roughly 64 scenarios. Its deterministic parts were exercised: the `needsConfirmation` flag, and the named failure phases and warnings that feed the repair loop. Omissions are counted in proportion to what they leave unexercised, and this share is not substantial. The other omissions (physical touchscreen, suites and lint, other widths) are disclosed and minor. Judge C's reason therefore does not reach the fail threshold, and I side with judges A and B.

audit_results.rationale: The quoted record shows broad coverage through public surfaces. It covers the reference sample in the production preview (steps, numbering, identity and departure, modes, keyboard, synthetic swipe, jumps, clamps and scaling) and the scaffold helper journeys. It also covers verify with a clean run and five fault runs, and inspect warnings, and round 2 re-explored the footer fix at 480, 360 and 320 px. Two things keep the quoted lines from deciding the pass. First, the approved specs, which define the user-visible behaviors to be covered, are not quoted. Without them a reviewer cannot judge how large a share of the behavior is left unexercised. Second, the ruling depends on the claim that the Floor G omissions are environmental, and the quoted lines do not establish that. The skill's conversational journeys are omitted: one question at a time, partial-detail build, ASCII mockup, ambiguous modify target, scoped modify, the agent repair loop and the confirmation gate. The record lists them under "Not exercised (deliberately)". It gives the reason "model dialogue, not product behaviour; this pass drove the deterministic scripts and the product". Its other wording, "requires a live agent session … this pass drove the deterministic scaffold helper, not the dialogue", does not say the environment lacked an agent invocation either. Both read as the candidate's own scoping choice, not a disclosed environmental impediment. Under the criterion, such omissions count against coverage in proportion to the user-visible behavior they leave unexercised. The quoted lines do not show whether that share is substantial, because the spec scenario basis is absent. Exercising the tool-level gates (the needsConfirmation flag, non-zero exits) checks a weaker property than the user-facing confirmation and repair scenarios. So the material neither confirms the pass nor clearly shows the fail threshold met.

lines.text: ## Is the `Step<unknown>` erasure at the `<Presentation>` boundary approved, or does it need a generic boundary and mismatch test?

- **Canonical scenario:** "Typed payloads reach presentation boundary": "WHEN a grouped scene defines steps with a strongly typed payload THEN the presentation host accepts that typed step array without requiring casts at the `<Presentation>` boundary".
- **Design, "Scene kit":** the generic `Step<TPayload>` and `SceneProps<TPayload>` "preserve strongly typed grouped payloads through the `<Presentation>` boundary without casts".

- **Code inspected:** `src/presentation-kit/types.ts` defines `Scene` with a bivariance hack, and `PresentationProps.steps` is `readonly Step[]`. `src/presentation-kit/types.test.tsx` has `@ts-expect-error` cases for mismatches at explicit `Step

` declarations and a no-cast acceptance test. The sample passes `STEPS: readonly Step[]` (`steps.ts:19`).

- **Ruling:** Compliant with the canonical scenario. No user decision is needed. The approved requirement is acceptance without casts, and that holds for homogeneous and mixed typed arrays. The design sentence is read as the same "without casts" guarantee. It does not require the boundary to reject mismatches. Reasons to keep the boundary non-generic:

- A presentation's steps may use different Scene components with different payloads (the `mixed` case in `types.test.tsx`). TypeScript has no existential per-element type, so a single `

` on `Presentation` would reject valid heterogeneous presentations.

- Payload and Scene agreement is enforced where authors declare a `Step

` (the sample does, via `Step`), and that is tested.

- **Accepted limitation:** An inline step literal written directly in the `steps` prop, with a Scene requiring `{stage}` and a payload `{label}`, is accepted. Rejecting it would add a mismatch guarantee that no approved sentence states. It is not a defect to report against the definition, and it should not be fixed as part of this change. If a reviewer wants it closed, a typed helper for declaring steps would be an addition, not a correction.

- **Checklist correction:** L-3 is verified for its approved content: typed arrays cross the boundary without casts, and `Step

` mismatches are rejected where declared. The lead row's sub-claim of "no `unknown` erasure" at the boundary is stricter than the definition. Record it as an accepted limitation in the evidence, not as a failure.
- **Pending user decision:** None. A user decision would be needed only if the user wants boundary-level mismatch rejection as a new requirement.

lines.text: ## Is the `Step<unknown>` erasure at the `<Presentation>` boundary approved, or does it need a generic boundary and mismatch test?

- **Canonical scenario:** "Typed payloads reach presentation boundary": "WHEN a grouped scene defines steps with a strongly typed payload THEN the presentation host accepts that typed step array without requiring casts at the `<Presentation>` boundary".
- **Design, "Scene kit":** the generic `Step<TPayload>` and `SceneProps<TPayload>` "preserve strongly typed grouped payloads through the `<Presentation>` boundary without casts".

- **Code inspected:** `src/presentation-kit/types.ts` defines `Scene` with a bivariance hack, and `PresentationProps.steps` is `readonly Step[]`. `src/presentation-kit/types.test.tsx` has `@ts-expect-error` cases for mismatches at explicit `Step

` declarations and a no-cast acceptance test. The sample passes `STEPS: readonly Step[]` (`steps.ts:19`).

- **Ruling:** Compliant with the canonical scenario. No user decision is needed. The approved requirement is acceptance without casts, and that holds for homogeneous and mixed typed arrays. The design sentence is read as the same "without casts" guarantee. It does not require the boundary to reject mismatches. Reasons to keep the boundary non-generic:

- A presentation's steps may use different Scene components with different payloads (the `mixed` case in `types.test.tsx`). TypeScript has no existential per-element type, so a single `

` on `Presentation` would reject valid heterogeneous presentations.

- Payload and Scene agreement is enforced where authors declare a `Step

` (the sample does, via `Step`), and that is tested.

- **Accepted limitation:** An inline step literal written directly in the `steps` prop, with a Scene requiring `{stage}` and a payload `{label}`, is accepted. Rejecting it would add a mismatch guarantee that no approved sentence states. It is not a defect to report against the definition, and it should not be fixed as part of this change. If a reviewer wants it closed, a typed helper for declaring steps would be an addition, not a correction.

- **Checklist correction:** L-3 is verified for its approved content: typed arrays cross the boundary without casts, and `Step

` mismatches are rejected where declared. The lead row's sub-claim of "no `unknown` erasure" at the boundary is stricter than the definition. Record it as an accepted limitation in the evidence, not as a failure.
- **Pending user decision:** None. A user decision would be needed only if the user wants boundary-level mismatch rejection as a new requirement.

verification-tooling.rationale: The contradiction holds. The fixture requires that the helper report no overlap warnings for elements inside a subtree marked as allowing overlap. `findOverlaps` skips a pair only when both elements share a marked ancestor id. A marked descendant that collides with an element outside the subtree has an empty `allow` list on the other side, so the pair is still reported, naming the marked element. That breaks the plain wording: the helper reports an overlap warning for an element inside the marked subtree. The review guidance names this marked-versus-unmarked scenario and calls skipping any pair with at least one marked element the correct reading. So this is not an unnamed hypothetical, and the code shows the behaviour directly. The focused tests (`fx-allowed`, `fx-mixed`) only cover collisions where both elements are marked, or both are unmarked chrome. Neither covers a marked element colliding with an unmarked one, so they cannot rescue the pass.

engineering-quality.rationale: The requirement demands termination of the preview server on every exit path, explicitly including an error after the preview started, and the guidance accepts cleanup only in a finally path every exit passes through. In both inspect copies the finally block runs await browser.close() then await preview.stop() sequentially with no nested try/finally, so a rejection from browser.close() (an error thrown after the preview started) skips preview.stop(), which is the only code that kills and awaits the Vite child. The verify copies are fine (renderRoute closes the browser in its own finally, and main's finally always calls preview.stop()), but the inspect copies alone defeat the pass verdict, whose rationale claimed cleanup covers subsequent operational errors.
evidence: scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs and skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs: the finally block is 'await browser.close()' followed by 'await preview.stop…
scripts/lib/project.mjs: the preview child is terminated (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL) and awaited only inside stop().
scripts/verify.mjs: main's finally calling preview.stop() is separate from renderRoute's finally calling browser.close(), so verify is not affected. The defect is in the inspect copies only.

engineering-quality.rationale: The criterion fails only when a readiness wait has no timeout. Both copies of startPreview have a timeout on their readiness wait: a deadline of 30000 ms (timeoutMs) that the polling loop checks on every pass, throwing 'preview not ready' once it passes. The auditor's point is that one fetch probe could stay pending, which needs a server that accepts the connection but never answers. That is a hypothetical input. The guidance does not name it, and the source and recorded evidence do not show it happening. If the preview child exits, the existing 'exited' check and the dropped connection end the probe. The other two clauses are also met. In both verify copies, main awaits runBuild and checks its exit code before it calls startPreview. Inspect also awaits the build before starting the preview. Readiness polls HTTP rather than parsing printed output, so the ANSI and chunked-output clause does not apply.
evidence: scripts/lib/project.mjs and the bootstrap copy: const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs with timeoutMs = 30000, and if (Date.now() > deadline) throw new Error('preview not ready ...') insi…
Readiness is an HTTP probe (await fetch(url + '/'), break on response.ok). It does not parse stdout, so the ANSI and chunk parsing clause does not apply.
scripts/verify.mjs and the bootstrap copy: await phase('build', ...) awaits runBuild and checks result.code before const preview = await startPreview(PROJECT_ROOT).
inspect-presentation.mjs (both copies): const build = await runBuild(PROJECT_ROOT) runs and is checked before startPreview.
A fetch that never settles needs a server that accepts but never answers. Neither the source nor the recorded evidence shows that, and the review guidance does not name it as a failing scenario.
